output_list.criticism: The 'Buy' function has an integer overflow vulnerability involving the variables 'amountToMint' and 'amountToReturn'. When 'stageIndex < 5 && stageMaxEthAmount > this.balance', 'amountToMint' is calculated as 'this.balance * (currS.stagePrice)'. If 'this.balance' is very large, 'amountToMint' can underflow and become zero, preventing 'mintCoins' from executing and allowing the attacker to always buy an out of bounds stage. Similarly, when 'status == 2 && stageIndex + 1 < 6 && stageMaxEthAmount > this.balance', 'amountToReturn' is set to '(stageMaxEthAmount - amountOfEthBeforeBuy) * (currS.stagePrice)'. If 'stageMaxEthAmount' and 'this.balance' are very large, 'amountToReturn' can underflow and become zero, preventing 'beneficiary.transfer(stageMaxEthAmount)' from executing and allowing the attacker to always buy an out of bounds stage.

The 'mintCoins' function has an integer overflow vulnerability involving the variable 'amountToMint'. When 'totalSupply.add(_amount) < maxTokenSupply', 'amountToMint' is set to 'this.balance * (currS.stagePrice)'. If 'this.balance' is very large, 'amountToMint' can underflow and become zero, preventing 'super.mint(_to,_amount.mul(75).div(100))' and 'super.mint(address(beneficiary),_amount.mul(25).div(100))' from executing, allowing the attacker to mint an excessively large token output.
